approaches.definition: Support for data curation and data management throughout the data life cycle. This includes efforts to clean data to assure consistency; organize and maintain datasets; support proper data documentation; and create metadata so these data can be accessed, used, and reused.

typical_examples.text: Interventions to strengthen data management, data quality assurance, and administration across the data life cycle, from data creation to processing, storing, transferring, archiving, and preservation, to disposal or destruction as appropriate
Interventions to support the cleaning or wrangling of datasets
Interventions to support or strengthen organization and maintenance of datasets

Interventions to support proper data documentation, which describes how the data were created, the structure of the data and its contents, and any cleaning or manipulation of the data to enhance quality or enable useability
Interventions to support or strengthen metadata or development of search functions for metadata
Interventions to support development or improvements to a data catalog
Interventions to support the development of a schedule for data management, retention, and/or possible disposal, as appropriate
Interventions to support or strengthen data interoperability.

third_level_themes.name: Data Management, Documentation, and Preservation
third_level_themes.definition: Support for data management at any point in (and across) the data life cycle: from data creation to processing, to storing, to data transfers, to archiving and preservation, to disposal or destruction as appropriate. This includes support for data documentation, metadata, database/data catalog management, and data preservation so these data can be accessed, used, and reused.

typical_examples.text: Interventions to strengthen data management and administration at any point in (or across) the data life cycle: from data creation to processing, to storing, to data transfers, to archiving and preservation, to disposal or destruction as appropriate
Interventions to support or strengthen organization and maintenance of datasets

Interventions to support proper data documentation, which describes how the data were created, the structure of the data and its contents, and any cleaning or manipulation of the data to enhance quality or enable useability
Interventions to support or strengthen metadata or development of search functions for metadata
Interventions to support development or improvements to a database or data catalog
Interventions to support the development of a schedule for data management, retention, and/or possible disposal, as appropriate.

third_level_themes.name: Data Cleaning, Consistency, Data Quality Assurance, and Data Interoperability
third_level_themes.definition: Support to clean data to enhance quality assurance and data consistency and to strengthen or enable data interoperability.

typical_examples.text: Interventions to support the cleaning or wrangling of datasets
Interventions to support data quality assurance
Interventions to strengthen syntactic data interoperability (for example, strengthening the structuring and formatting of data to be used in the exchange of information)
Interventions to strengthen data systems semantic interoperability (for example, strengthening interoperability of registries or information systems)
Interventions to support the development or strengthening of interoperability frameworks or interoperability agreements.

approaches.relevant_global_practices: AGF, CCG, DD, ENB, FCI, FCV, GEN, GOV, HNP, IFC, IPG, JBS, MTI, POV, SPJ, SSI, URL, WTR

approaches.definition: Support for systems or processes to strengthen data dissemination, data accessibility, and discoverability of data.

typical_examples.text: Interventions to develop or strengthen management information systems (MISs), such as education or higher education (EMIS/HEMIS), geospatial information systems, disaster risk information systems, climate data/information systems, health (HMIS), Labor (LMIS), social information systems, and more

Interventions to support core government data systems which support the key functions of collecting, processing, and managing records and data and which enable upstream functions, such as public financial management (revenue, expenditures, and debt), e-government procurement, human resource management, and central and local government operations

Development of an open data portal or platform or support for a broader open data initiative, including support to make government data publicly available, free of charge, without restrictions, in machine-readable formats, and reusable formats, with their associated metadata
Development of a website or dashboards for data dissemination and use by the public or by targeted/authorized user groups (for example, ministry staff)

Development of citizen engagement platforms, including CivicTech solutions, to enable citizen participation and the sharing of citizen-generated data, citizen surveys, open government, and open data platforms to improve accountability and reporting/ web publishing
Interventions to develop or strengthen data dissemination strategies or release calendars
Interventions to strengthen data discoverability, which enable users to easily locate available data, detect their quality, understand their structure and lineage, and access them.

third_level_themes.name: Data Platforms, Websites, Dashboards, or Information Systems (MISs)
third_level_themes.definition: Data platforms, websites, or dashboards to enable data dissemination, accessibility, and discoverability by government and nongovernment actors.

typical_examples.text: Interventions to develop or strengthen management information systems (MISs), such as education (EMIS/HEMIS); geospatial information systems; disaster risk information systems; climate data/ information systems; health (HMIS); Labor (LMIS); social information systems; and more

Development of an open data portal or platform or support for a broader open data initiative, including support to make government data publicly available, free of charge, without restrictions, in machine-readable formats and reusable formats, with their associated metadata.

Data Maturity Assessment
Data availability diagnostic (for example, assessment of data quality or availability against the Data for Policy [D4P] minimum package)
Data/statistical skills assessment

Assessment of economic impact of data production, adoption, and use.

Sectoral data strategies, such as a gender data strategy, an agricultural data strategy, an education data strategy, or climate data strategy

Support for the operationalization of a social contract for data.

third_level_themes.name: Data Rights
third_level_themes.definition: Support for the development or implementation of data rights, data empowerment, or data sovereignty reforms.

typical_examples.text: Interventions to support or strengthen awareness of the concept of data rights, that is, a rights-based approach for the public to understand and exercise discretion over where their personal data go and how they are used

Interventions to support or strengthen awareness of the concept of data sovereignty, that is, a group’s or individual’s right to control and maintain their own data, such as across data collection and data storage activities, and/or the interpretation of their data

Interventions to support or strengthen awareness of the concept of data portability, that is, to enable a group or individuals to receive—or transmit to another controller on their behalf— personal data they have provided to a controller in a structured, commonly used, and machine-readable format.

approaches.approach_name: Literacy and Capacity Building On Data
approaches.definition: Support to develop or strengthen human or institutional capacity at the national or subnational level, to enable increased quality, quantity, dissemination, and use of data or statistics for social, economic, and/or sustainable development. “Capacity building” describes support activities designed to enhance the skills or individual agency of government or nongovernment stakeholders to collect, manage, govern, safeguard, analyze, disseminate, or use data or statistics. “Institutional strengthening” describes support activities designed to develop or strengthen national or subnational government or parastatal administrative or coordination agencies or entities that collect, process, analyze, or use data or statistics.

typical_examples.text: Interventions to build capacity or strengthen individual agency of government or nongovernment actors on data or statistics, for example,
sub: Any training on statistics (sampling, statistical analysis, econometrics, and so on)
Any training on data literacy and data use (workshops, data fellowships, hackathons, and so on)
Support to create/strengthen data communities of practice.

typical_examples.text: Interventions to create or strengthen an institution or institutional arrangement to support data or statistics activities, for example,
sub: Creation, designation, or strengthening of an autonomous intergovernment administrative or coordination agency (or national institute for statistics) with the responsibility of oversight and implementation of collection, processing, analysis, or use of data or statistics

Development or strengthening of a data governance institution, which might, for example, be responsible for strategic planning, rulemaking or rule implementation, compliance, or learning/ evidence generation for data or statistics activities
Establishment or strengthening of an enabling or safeguarding institution in the public sector, such as a public entity focused on GovTech reforms.

typical_examples.text: Interventions to strengthen data ethics, that is, to support or strengthen data producers’ or data users’ responsible data acquisition, management, use, and disposal in line with best practice approaches, for example,
sub: Training to strengthen support, transparency, and accountability in the use of artificial intelligence (AI) and automated decision-making systems in the public sector
Workshops to train government data scientists or data managers in responsible data use
Training to enable researchers to adopt open science or open code approaches, that is, by publishing the source code of algorithms in public registers.
